questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Temples as Living Architecture' refers to.
questions.a: Indian temples are stone records of faith and craft - from the stepwell Rani ki Vav and the hill shrine of Hidimba Devi with its timber style to towering gopurams - each region developing its own temple architecture shaped by local material and worship.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Temples as Living Architecture'.
questions.a: Temple architecture varies by region and material, but everywhere it joins devotion with engineering.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Temples as Living Architecture' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: hees203.txt lines 130-180 (Rani ki Vav, Hidimba Devi temple, Sharada Peeth temple))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Mosques, Forts and Sultanate-Mughal Building' refers to.
questions.a: The coming of Islamic architecture brought the arch, dome and minaret: grand mosques like the Jama Masjid of Delhi and Ahmedabad, along with forts and tombs, blended Persian ideas with Indian craftsmanship to create an Indo-Islamic style.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Mosques, Forts and Sultanate-Mughal Building'.
questions.a: Arch, dome and minaret met Indian carving to build the Indo-Islamic synthesis.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Mosques, Forts and Sultanate-Mughal Building' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: hees203.txt lines 137-175 (Jama Masjid Ahmedabad, Jama Masjid Delhi))

concepts.title: Colonial Architecture: Havelis to High Courts

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Colonial Architecture: Havelis to High Courts' refers to.
questions.a: Colonial times added their own layer - merchant havelis of Shekhawati with frescoed courtyards, and grand public buildings such as the Madras High Court - where classical European facades adapted to Indian climate and craft.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Colonial Architecture: Havelis to High Courts'.
questions.a: Colonial architecture grafted European styles onto Indian builders and settings.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Colonial Architecture: Havelis to High Courts' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 3 (source: hees203.txt lines 79-95 (Madras High Court, Havelis of Shekhawati), 169-175)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Reading Monuments as Historical Sources' refers to.
questions.a: Monuments are history written in stone: inscriptions, plans and styles reveal a building's patron, period, technology and religious life, so a journey through Indian architecture is a journey through India's past itself.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Reading Monuments as Historical Sources'.
questions.a: Every pillar and inscription is a document - monuments testify about their times.
